requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, then daemon-reload and enable --now were run. systemctl status confirms active/enabled with MainPID 1978 running the binary, and the process tree shows the worker script executing under the unit. This state persisted through a subsequent reboot (MainPID 737 post-restart), confirming durable, correctly-configured service management.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: Pre-check confirmed no inventorysvc account existed beforehand (cmd-316385eff30e40a4). A system account inventorysvc (uid 992, no home, nologin shell) was created via useradd --system, and the unit sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc with NoNewPrivileges=true. Process ownership (ps -o user) shows the worker running as 'invento+' (inventorysvc) both immediately after start and after the reboot, with the account still intact post-restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — running os-comparison-worker as a systemd service named inventory-worker, and running it under a dedicated inventorysvc account — are directly and fully satisfied, with evidence both immediately after configuration and again after a full node restart, confirming durability. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id/service baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, timeout-then-success polling proving disconnection/reconnection, a changed boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of the service and account, corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary mutations, residue, failed services, or exposure changes were introduced.
limitations: No evidence was captured of the worker script's actual runtime output/logs beyond process presence; only process ownership and systemd state were verified, which is sufficient for the stated requirements but does not confirm application-level correctness of the binary's behavior.

The single reboot acknowledgement command returned return_code -1 with 'exec stream closed before command completion', which is expected behavior for a reboot command losing its connection, not a failure indicator.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were read-only discovery (cmd-316385eff30e40a4, cmd-2571cc9baecf4f45, cmd-4e53578930a5496f, cmd-7564af84af54474a, cmd-2b39190fa1b94d2f, cmd-b36236d8ed034a40, cmd-dab04d4763e9495a) except for the account/service creation (cmd-19d68079d5a14bfc) and the reboot (cmd-c909a7aceb684a50), both of which are directly tied to the task outcome and to the independently-required node-restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. Global lifecycle diffs between after-prepare and after-executor show only expected changes: boot_id change from the reboot, ephemeral systemd-private temp dirs regenerated under the new boot_id (not user-created residue), and socket entries differing only by PID (same services: sshd, chronyd) with no new listeners. No failed services and no package-health regressions were observed after the executor's work.
